sources.title: Can I trust the polls? And other questions from listeners about the 2026 midterms
'Atmosphere of fear': Trump moves to curtail voting rights ahead of the midterms

en.title: Trump Announces Voting Restrictions Ahead of 2026 Midterms
en.dek: President Trump pushes for new voting rules citing concerns over noncitizen voting.
facts: Trump has been pushing lawmakers to pass the Safeguard American Voter Eligibility (SAVE) Act.
The SAVE Act would require documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to vote.
Trump has repeatedly claimed large numbers of noncitizens are voting, but Heritage Foundation data shows only 100 cases from 1982‑2025.
Campaign Legal Center reports more than 21 million Americans lack documentary proof of citizenship.
AP‑NORC poll shows 55% of Democrats and 38% of Republicans feel confident in midterm vote accuracy.
body: On October 22, 2026, President Donald Trump spoke at a rally at Sioux Gateway Airport in Sioux City, Iowa.

Trump has a history of challenging unfavorable election results, notably blaming his 2020 defeat on alleged fraud, and he has repeatedly claimed that large numbers of noncitizens are voting in U.S. elections.
According to the Campaign Legal Center, the Trump administration has tried to insert the federal government into almost every aspect of the election process.
Trump is pushing lawmakers to pass the Safeguard American Voter Eligibility (SAVE) Act.
The SAVE Act would require voters to present documentary proof of U.S. citizenship.
Acceptable IDs would include a U.S. passport, a military ID card, a government‑issued photo ID showing birth in the United States, or a birth certificate that matches the current name exactly.
The Act would exclude driver’s licenses or other IDs that do not indicate place of birth, which could affect voters who changed names after marriage or are transgender.
Trump claims that noncitizens are voting in large numbers, but the actual numbers are exceedingly rare.
Voting in U.S. elections is reserved for citizens and requires an ID; noncitizens who attempt to vote can face fines, prison, or deportation.

The Heritage Foundation’s database lists 100 cases of noncitizen voting from 1982 to 2025, representing about 0.000008 percent of more than 1.3 billion votes cast in presidential elections during that period.
The Campaign Legal Center reports that more than 21 million Americans, or nearly 10 percent of voting‑age Americans, lack access to documentary proof of citizenship.
The lack of proof disproportionately affects young people, low‑income individuals, and people of color.
An Associated Press‑NORC Center poll found that 55 percent of Democrats and 38 percent of Republicans feel confident that the final midterm count will be accurate.
Jonathan Diaz, director for voting advocacy and partnerships at the Campaign Legal Center, said the Trump administration’s actions have created an atmosphere of fear and uncertainty.
The Trump administration has also tried to influence state and local election officials, but many attempts have failed.
en.context: The 2026 midterm elections could shift control of Congress, affecting President Trump's legislative agenda. Trump has previously challenged election outcomes and sought to influence election rules. The new voting restrictions are part of his strategy to protect his agenda.
